newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco mulling Malaysia refinery site.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco mulling Malaysia refinery site.

text.p: Australian bauxite miner and aluminium and alumina producer Comalco Ltd said on Monday it considered Malaysia the best alternative to Queensland as the location for its planned A$1 billion alumina refinery.

"We have zeroed in on Malaysia at the moment and I think that clearly is the place where we think we have the best alternative to the Queensland site," Comalco chief executive Terry Palmer told reporters.
But Palmer said the suitability of any alternative sites for the one million tonne-per-annum project largely hinged on the cost and security of supply of energy inputs, particularly gas.
"(Alternative sites) do some things to make them attractive and, in our case, if a country has copious quantities of pretty keenly-priced gas then that can help a lot," Palmer said.
He noted energy costs in an alumina refinery accounted for about a third of total operating costs.
Palmer said currently no site was favoured and the company was at an information gathering stage in Malaysia.

"We've had teams in Malaysia looking very seriously at just where the gas is, what all the other arrangements are. Because we've been in Queensland for so long we're much more familiar with that detail," he said.

Queensland's abundant gas resources made it a viable location for the refinery but the state's failure thus far to free up its energy market means spare electricity generated by the project might lack ready buyers.

"The market's not free and open there at the moment. So what we're talking to the Queensland government (about) is what sort of arrangements could be made to cover ourselves for that," Palmer said. He said the project feasibility study continued with a decision hoped for within weeks.
